name.text: Interpret the text and use the information to calculate conditional probabilities

questiontext.text:
(a) A garage sells three types of fuel; V-Power, Super and diesel. In a survey of {@motorists@} motorists buying fuel at the garage, {@female_motorists@} are female and the rest are male. Of the {@v_power@} motorists buying ‘V-Power’ fuel, {@female_v@} were female and of the {@diesel_fuel@} motorists buying diesel, {@male_diesel@} were male. A motorist does not buy more than one type of fuel.

Find the probability that a randomly chosen motorist

i. buys Super fuel: [[input:ans1]](rounded off to 2 decimal places) [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

ii. is male given that the motorist buys Super fuel: [[input:ans2]](rounded off to 2 decimal places)[[validation:ans2]][[feedback:prt2]]

(b) The garage records indicate that {@v_power_car_servived@}% of the motorists buying V-Power fuel, {@super_fuel_car_servived@}% of the motorists buying Super fuel, and {@diesel_fuel_car_servived@}% of the motorists buying diesel have their car serviced by the garage. A motorist is chosen at random

i. Find the probability that this motorist has his or her car serviced by the garage: [[input:ans3]](rounded off to 2 decimal places)[[validation:ans3]][[feedback:prt3]]

ii. Given the motorist has his or her car serviced by the garage, find the probability that the motorist buys diesel fuel: [[input:ans4]](rounded off to 2 decimal places)[[validation:ans4]][[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked out solution

Part (a).

Before we begin answering this question, let's take a moment and summarize the information provided in the question.

Total motorists = {@motorists@}

Female motorists = {@female_motorists@}

Male motorists = {@motorists@}- {@female_motorists@} = {@male_motorists@}

Fuel type

V-power

Super

Diesel

number of motorists buying

{@v_power@}

{@motorists@}-({@v_power@}+{@diesel_fuel@})={@super_fuel@}

{@diesel_fuel@}

Male motorists

{@v_power@}-{@female_v@}= {@male_v@}

{@male_motorists@}-({@male_v@}+{@male_diesel@})={@male_super_fuel@}

{@male_diesel@}

Female motorists

{@female_v@}

{@super_fuel@}-{@male_super_fuel@}= {@female_super_fuel@}

{@diesel_fuel@}-{@male_diesel@}={@female_diesel@}


From here, we can compute:

(i) Probability that a randomly chosen motorist buys Super fuel.

\(P(\mbox{Buy Super fuel})=\frac{\mbox{total number of motorists buying Super fuel}}{\mbox{total number of motorists}}= \frac{@super_fuel@}{@motorists@}={@ta1@}\)

(ii) Probability that a randomly chosen motorist is male given that the motorist buys Super fuel

Recall that this is a conditional probability and can be expressed as follows;

\(\text{P(Male|Buys super fuel)}=\frac{\text{Number of motorists who are male buying Super fuel}}{\text{Total number of motorists buying super fuel}}= \frac{@male_super_fuel@}{@super_fuel@} = {@ta2@} \)

Part (b)

Let us summarize the proportion of motorists who visit the garage as follows;

Type of fuel bought by the motorist

V-power

Super

Diesel

Proportion visiting the garage

{@v_power_car_servived@}% of {@v_power@} ={@v_power_car_servived*v_power/100@}

{@super_fuel_car_servived@}% of {@super_fuel@} = {@super_fuel_car_servived*super_fuel/100@}

{@diesel_fuel_car_servived@}% of {@diesel_fuel@} = {@diesel_fuel_car_servived*diesel_fuel/100@}

The proportion of motorists who have their cars serviced in the garage will be {@car_serviced@}

(i) Probability that a motorist has his or her car serviced by the garage.

\( P(\mbox{Car serviced by the garage})=\frac{@car_serviced@}{@motorists@}={@ta3@} \)

(ii) Probability that the motorist buys diesel fuel given his or her car is serviced by the garage

\(P(\mbox{Buys diesel|Car serviced by the garage})=\frac{P(\mbox{Buys diesel and has car serviced by the garage})}{P(\mbox{Car serviced by the garage})}\), which is equivalent to

\(P(\mbox{Buys diesel|Car serviced by the garage})=\frac{\mbox{Proportion of motorists who bought diesel visiting the garage}}{\mbox{Proportion of motorists who has their cars serviced in the garage}}\)

\(P(\mbox{Buys diesel|Car serviced by the garage})=\frac{@diesel_fuel_car_servived*diesel_fuel/100@}{@car_serviced@}= {@ta4@}\)
